packs.title: River, Road and Stories
packs.promise: Explore Tulsa parks, Route 66, wildlife and collections across separate outings.

q.s: Compare a designed play landscape with the Arkansas River edge.
st: Find a legal park view or its official map.
Describe one designed landform and one view toward the river.
Explain how a path connects the two without entering water.

q.s: Compare an animal exhibit with a natural habitat need.
st: Choose one species from an open exhibit or official zoo page.
Name one habitat feature visible or described.
Explain which animal need that feature supports, without feeding or approaching animals.

q.s: Compare a Tulsa history object with an archival image.
st: Choose one object or exhibit image from the museum or official site.
Find one archival image with a related theme.
Write one match and one difference between their evidence.

packs.title: Arts District and Greenwood
packs.promise: Follow connected Arts District and Greenwood streets in two afternoons.

q.s: Follow a public path across Guthrie Green and compare its lawn and stage.
st: Find a public view or operator image of the lawn and stage.
Describe how the two spaces support different activities.
Note one accessible path or shaded edge.

q.s: Study how one contemporary craft work uses material and form.
st: Choose one current gallery work or official online work.
Name its material and one form choice without touching it.
Explain how that choice changes the viewer’s impression.

q.s: Observe how Reconciliation Park’s open space and memorial forms invite reflection.
st: Enter by an open public path or read the official park account.
Describe one memorial form and the space around it.
Write a private reflection on what the site asks visitors to remember; do not photograph other visitors.
